meta.name: Correlate mobile crash reports with GitHub commits using Claude and Slack

name: AI Mobile Crash → Code Correlation Agent

parameters.content:
## AI Mobile Crash → Code Correlation Agent

Listens for new crash reports (webhook from Crashlytics/Sentry/Bugsnag), parses the stack trace to find the crashing file(s)/function(s)/line(s), pulls recent GitHub commit and PR history for those exact files, asks Claude to correlate the crash against the code-change history and name the most likely responsible commit/PR with a confidence level and reasoning, then opens a developer task (Jira/Linear/ClickUp style) pre-loaded with the crash context, stack trace, and the suspected diff — and pings the likely-responsible author directly on Slack.

### How to set up
1. Import this workflow into n8n
2. Add credentials: crash reporting webhook secret (if verifying signatures), GitHub API, Anthropic API (header auth, x-api-key), Jira/Linear/ClickUp API, Slack API
3. Edit Set - Config: repoOwner, repoName, taskProviderListId/projectId, slackChannelId, anthropicModel, lookbackDays, minConfidenceForAutoAssign
4. Activate the workflow (webhook goes live), or use the Manual Trigger with sample crash JSON to test end to end

### Requirements
- Crash reporting tool with outbound webhook support (Crashlytics, Sentry, Bugsnag, etc.)
- GitHub API access (commits, PRs, file blame/history)
- Anthropic API access (Claude)
- Developer task tool API access (Jira, Linear, or ClickUp)
- Slack API access (bot token, chat:write)

### How to customize
- Swap the crash-webhook parsing logic if your crash tool's payload shape differs (Crashlytics vs Sentry vs Bugsnag all differ)
- Adjust lookbackDays to control how far back in git history to search for suspicious changes
- Tune minConfidenceForAutoAssign to decide when to auto-assign vs just flag a suspected author
- Add crash-clustering (group by stack trace fingerprint) upstream to avoid opening duplicate tasks for the same root cause
- Feed resolved-task outcomes back into future prompts so Claude's correlation confidence calibrates over time

nodes.name: Sticky Note - Trigger & Stack Trace Parsing

parameters.content:
## 1. Trigger & Stack Trace Parsing

Webhook - New Crash Report receives the crash payload from your crash reporting tool (also works via Manual Trigger + Set - Sample Crash Payload for testing).

Set - Config centralizes repo details, task list/project id, Slack channel, and thresholds.

JS - Parse Stack Trace & Extract Frames normalizes whatever shape the crash tool sent into a consistent list of stack frames (file, function, line number), identifies the app-owned frames (filtering out OS/SDK/third-party library frames), and picks the top candidate frame(s) most likely to be the actual crash site.

## 2. Pull Code-Change History For Crashing Files

For each candidate crashing file, two parallel calls hit GitHub:
- HTTP Request - Fetch File Commit History: recent commits touching that exact file path, within lookbackDays
- HTTP Request - Fetch File Blame: current blame/line-authorship so Claude knows who last touched the exact crashing line

Merge - Combine Commit History & Blame joins both so the correlation prompt has full context: who changed this file recently, what they changed, and who owns the specific line.

## 3. AI Root-Cause Correlation

HTTP Request - Claude: Correlate Crash With Code Changes sends the parsed stack trace, the candidate crashing frames, and the commit/blame history and asks Claude to identify the single most likely responsible commit (or PR), a confidence score, its reasoning, a plain-language explanation of the likely bug, and a suggested fix direction.

JS - Parse Correlation Result parses that safely. IF - Confidence Meets Auto-Assign Threshold splits high-confidence correlations (auto-assign to the suspected author) from lower-confidence ones (task created but left unassigned for a human to triage).

## 4. Developer Task Creation & Notification

HTTP Request - Create Task (High Confidence) opens a task pre-assigned to the suspected author, with the crash context, stack trace, suspected commit/PR link, and Claude's reasoning baked into the description.

HTTP Request - Create Task (Needs Triage) opens the same task shape but unassigned, flagged for manual review.

Both branches converge into Slack - Notify Likely Responsible Author / Channel, which pings the suspected author directly (high confidence) or posts to a triage channel (low confidence) with a link to the new task.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ model: $json.anthropicModel, max_tokens: 1500, system: "You are a senior mobile engineer doing root-cause correlation for a crash report. You are given the exception type/message, the parsed stack trace, the candidate crashing frames (files/functions/lines most likely responsible, filtered to app-owned code), and recent commit history plus last-known-author evidence for each candidate file. Respond with ONLY a JSON object: { mostLikelyResponsible: { file: string, commitSha: string|null, author: string, commitMessage: string|null, commitUrl: string|null }, confidencePercent: number, reasoning: string, likelyBugExplanation: string, suggestedFixDirection: string, alternativeSuspects: [ { file: string, author: string, reason: string } ] }. Base confidence on how directly a recent commit's message/diff timing plausibly relates to the crashing line and exception type; if nothing correlates well, still name the most plausible file/author but keep confidencePercent low.", messages: [ { role: "user", content: JSON.stringify({ exceptionType: $json.exceptionType, exceptionMessage: $json.exceptionMessage, platform: $json.platform, appVersion: $json.appVersion, fullStackTrace: $json.fullStackTrace, evidenceByFrame: $json.evidenceByFrame }, null, 2) } ] }) }}
